extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, opponents, patent agents/attorneys, and patent office officials practising in India
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing post-grant matters under Indian patent law: oppositions, hearings, renewals, restoration, assignments, surrender, working/compulsory licensing, revocation, appeals and register maintenance. Includes timelines, filing/formalities, grounds, evidence limits and decision criteria administered by the Controller, Opposition Board, Appellate Board, IPAB and Central Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for post-grant opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-grant opposition can be filed on the grounds as mentioned in Section 25(2), but no other grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions are restricted to the statutory grounds listed in Section 25(2); other grounds are not permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to file opposition (who may oppose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponent may be any person interested, e.g., an organization with a manufacturing or trading interest in the goods connected with the patented article, a person with a financial interest in manufacturing such goods, or one who possesses patents relating to the same subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Opposition must include a statement setting out the nature of the opponent's interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and document filing requirements for opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of Notice of Opposition, the Controller shall notify the patentee; copies of all documents referred to in the Notice or any statement/evidence must be furnished in duplicate and duly authenticated; a copy of the statement and evidence, if any, shall be delivered to the patentee by the opponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents should be originals or duly notarized. Where documents are in a language other than English, an attested English translation in duplicate must be furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee's reply timeline and consequence of non-reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee desires to contest the opposition, he shall file a reply statement and evidence within two months from receipt of the copy of the opponent's written statement and evidence, and deliver a copy to the opponent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patentee does not file his reply and evidence within two months, the patent shall be deemed to have been revoked and the Controller shall issue the order of revocation and enter revocation in the register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opponent's reply timeline and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of the patentee's reply, the opponent may file his reply statement and evidence within one month from the date of delivery of a copy of the patentee's reply statement and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply evidence of the opponent shall be strictly confined to the matters in the patentee’s evidence; the opponent shall deliver a copy to the patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further evidence restrictions and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: No further evidence shall be delivered by either party, except with the leave or direction of the Controller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further evidence, if allowed, shall be filed before the Controller's notification fixing the date of hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification or other document in a language other than English is referred to in notice, statement or evidence, an attested translation thereof in duplicate in English should be furnished along with such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitution of Opposition Board
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of Notice of Opposition, an Opposition Board is constituted by the Controller to examine the notice and documents filed under rules 57-60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Opposition Board consists of three members with one as Chairman; the examiner may be a member, but the examiner who dealt with the application during prosecution shall not be a member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Board report timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall submit a report with reasons on each ground taken in the Notice of Opposition as a joint recommendation within three months from the date on which all documents were forwarded to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If further evidence is taken on record by the Controller, it shall be forwarded to the Board for consideration (also applies to evidence taken after receipt of Board report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing notice period and fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the Opposition Board's recommendation the Controller shall fix a date and time for hearing and inform the parties at least ten days in advance. On receipt of the notice, if a party desires to be heard, he shall inform the Controller by a notice along with the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Controller may refuse to hear any party which has not given such notice and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for relying on additional publications at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If either party intends to rely on any publication at the hearing not already mentioned, he shall give notice of his intention together with details at least five days before the date of hearing to the other party and the Controller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller's decision outcomes in opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: After hearing parties or if neither desires to be heard, and after considering the Board recommendation, the Controller may revoke the patent, order amendments in the patent, or refuse the opposition and issue a speaking order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendment is ordered, the patentee shall submit amended documents within a reasonable time as directed by the Controller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal fee timing and payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees are payable at the expiration of the second year from the date of the patent or of any succeeding year and should be remitted before the expiration of that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First renewal fee becomes due in respect of the third year counted from date of filing; for patents granted later than two years from filing, fees which became due may be paid within three months from recording of patent; the patentee must correctly quote patent number, date and year when paying; Patent of Addition requires no renewal fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended period for renewal payments (late payment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal of a patent can be done beyond the due date in the extended period of six months from that date by filing Form-4 along with prescribed fee; this six-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a patent is granted after two years from filing, renewal fees due in the meantime may be paid within three months of recording; extension period also applied as maximum six months by filing Form-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration application eligibility and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent has ceased due to non-payment of renewal fees, restoration may be applied for by the patentee/assignee/legal representative by filing Form 15 within eighteen months from the date on which the patent ceased to have effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of joint applicants, with Controller's leave any one or more may apply without joining others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration supporting statement and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must state the circumstances which led to the failure of payment and include a statement fully setting out the circumstances; this may be supported by evidence and copies of documents referred to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must support that failure to pay was unintentional and there has been no undue delay; Controller may call for further evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration name-change and identity formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: If patentee failed to register a change of name before cessation he must first apply under Rule 94 for alteration in the register; if changed name after cessation he must prove identity and draw/sign application in new name adding 'formerly known as' as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for disposal of restoration application
rubrics_metrics.description: If Controller is prima facie satisfied that failure to pay was unintentional and no undue delay, the application will be published in official journal; if not satisfied, Controller may issue notice and allow request for hearing within one month or refuse the application and issue a speaking order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person interested may oppose within two months of publication; when no opposition or opposition disposed, Controller issues order allowing restoration and unpaid renewal plus additional fee must be paid within one month from date of order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for third parties between lapse and restoration publication
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect persons who began to use the invention between the date the patent ceased and the date of publication of the restoration application, every order for restoration includes provisions/conditions for protection and compensation of those persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No suit or proceeding for infringement shall be commenced for infringement committed between the date patent ceased and date of publication of the application for restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for registration of assignments/transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment or share, mortgage, licence or creation of any other interest in a patent shall be valid only if in writing and reduced to a document embodying all terms and duly executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person entitled may apply in Form-16 to the Controller for registration of title or notice of interest; Controller enters particulars upon proof of title to his satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller discretion where disputes in title exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is any dispute between the parties, the Controller may refuse to take action to make an entry in the register until rights are determined by a competent court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for registration purposes or rectification proceedings, an unregistered document shall not be admitted by Controller or any court as evidence of title unless Controller/court for reasons in writing otherwise directs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrender of patent procedure and opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee may offer to surrender patent by application; Controller publishes the offer and notifies persons having interest in the register; opposition may be filed in Form-14 within 3 months from publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for written statements, reply, evidence and hearing is similar to post-grant opposition; if Controller accepts surrender, he may direct return of patent and revoke it and publish revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to work patents in India (working of patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are granted to encourage inventions which should be worked in full within India; inventions should be worked on a commercial scale and to the fullest extent reasonably practicable without undue delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents are not granted merely to enable patentees to enjoy monopoly for importation; patent rights shall not be abused; inventions should be available at reasonably affordable prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and Form 27 annual working statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Controller may call for periodical statements as to the extent to which the patented invention has been commercially worked in India; a patentee or licensee shall furnish such information within two months from date of notice; details of working must be furnished in Form 27 for every calendar year within three months of year end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to supply may attract Controller action under Section 146(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after grant — scope and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: After grant, the patentee may apply in Form-13 for amendment of application, complete specification or any related document; request shall state nature of proposed amendment and reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are allowable only by way of disclaimer, correction or explanation and only to incorporate actual fact; no amendment shall claim or describe matter not in substance disclosed before amendment; amended pages filed in duplicate with cancelled originals; substantive amendments are published and open to opposition within three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud in obtaining leave to amend is ground for revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A leave to amend the complete specification obtained by fraud is a ground for revocation of patent under Section 64.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suit for infringement or revocation proceedings pending, Controller shall not pass order allowing or refusing application for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure on death of applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant died before grant but patent was granted in his name, a person who ought to have patent may request Controller to substitute name via Form-10; if applicant dies after grant, any person entitled by operation of law may request registration of title in Form-16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of patents contents and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Register contains details about patentee, notifications of assignments, transmissions, licences, amendments, extension and revocations; certified copies or extracts are admissible in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On grant, Controller enters names, addresses, nationality, title, categories, date of patent, date of granting, address for service and fact of renewal fee payment; particulars of proceedings before Controller or courts are entered; additional address for service (max two) may be entered; register available publicly at each Patent Office and on official website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of register grounds and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for rectification of register may be made to IPAB by any person aggrieved by absence/omission of entry, by any entry made without sufficient cause, by any entry wrongly remaining, or by any error or defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of such application is given to Controller who is entitled to be heard; if IPAB rectifies, Controller is served notice and rectifies the register accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealable decisions and locus of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal lies from decisions, orders or directions made under the Patents Act by the Central Government or any act/order of the Controller for giving effect to such decisions; appeal also lies from Controller/Central Government under specified sections (15,16,17,18,19,20,25(4),28,51,54,57,60,61,63,66,69(3),78,84(1)-(5),85,88,91,92,94).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appeal lies from an Order of the Controller granting extension of time where such extension is provided in any provision of the Act or rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedural requirements and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Every appeal from Controller's decision must be accompanied by a certified copy of the decision and be in the prescribed form with fee; every appeal should be made within three months from date of decision or within further time as Appellate Board may allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller has the right to appear and be heard and may submit a written statement in lieu of appearance; Appellate Board may direct Controller to appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation before Appellate Board or High Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person interested including the Central Government may petition on grounds specified under Section 64 for revocation before the Appellate Board; a patent may be revoked by the High Court on a counter-claim in a suit for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central Government may also petition High Court to revoke if patentee has without reasonable cause failed to comply with request to make/use invention for government purposes under Section 99.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation by Controller on Central Government direction (atomic energy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Central Government is satisfied that a patent is for an invention relating to atomic energy for which no patent can be granted, it may direct Controller to revoke the patent; Controller shall give notice and opportunity to be heard and may revoke or allow amendment instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller may permit amendment of the complete specification instead of revocation where he considers it necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation by Central Government for public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Central Government is of opinion that a patent or its mode of exercise is mischievous to the State or generally prejudicial to the public, it may, after giving patentee opportunity to be heard, make a declaration in the Official Gazette and the patent shall be deemed revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation by Controller for non-working (post-compulsory licence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a compulsory licence has been granted, Central Government or any person interested may apply to Controller for order revoking the patent on grounds that the invention has not been worked in India, reasonable public requirements not satisfied, or invention not available at reasonably affordable price; such application only after expiration of two years from order granting first compulsory licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application should contain prescribed particulars and facts and, if not by Central Government, nature of applicant's interest; such applications ordinarily decided within one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles guiding working and compulsory licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents should be worked in India on commercial scale to fullest extent reasonably practicable without undue delay; patents not granted solely to enable monopoly for importation; protection/enforcement should promote technological innovation, transfer and public interest (health/nutrition), and patent rights should not be abused to unreasonably restrain trade or adversely affect technology transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patented inventions should be made available at reasonably affordable prices and interests of persons working/developing inventions under patent should not be unfairly prejudiced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence under Section 84 — eligibility and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person interested may apply to Controller for grant of compulsory licence after expiry of three years from date of grant on grounds that (i) reasonable requirements of public not satisfied, (ii) invention not available at reasonably affordable price, or (iii) invention not worked in territory of India. Licensee may also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person estopped from alleging these grounds by prior admission or acceptance of licence; Controller considers nature of invention, elapsed time since sealing, measures by patentee to make full use, applicant's ability to work invention, applicant's capacity to undertake risk/capital, and whether applicant tried to obtain licence on reasonable terms (reasonable period ordinarily not exceeding six months) except in national emergency, extreme urgency, public noncommercial use, or anti-competitive practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'reasonable requirements of the public' (Section 84(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable requirements deemed not satisfied if: I. refusal to grant licence prejudices existing/developing trade or industry or demand not met to adequate extent or export market not supplied/developed or establishment/development of commercial activities in India prejudiced; II. conditions imposed by patentee on grant of licences or purchase/use of patented article/process prejudice manufacture/use/sale of non-protected materials or establishment/development of trade/industry; III. patentee imposes exclusive grant-back, prevention to challenges or coercive package licensing; IV. invention not being worked in India on commercial scale to adequate extent or fullest extent reasonably practicable; V. working in India on commercial scale is prevented or hindered by importation from abroad by patentee or persons claiming under him or persons buying from him or others against whom patentee is not taking proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a compulsory licence application
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must contain a statement setting out nature of applicant's interest, facts upon which application is based and terms and conditions of the licence the applicant is willing to accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for compulsory licence applications and opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If Controller satisfied prima facie case made out, he shall direct applicant to serve copies on patentee and persons interested and publish application in official journal; patentee/other person may oppose within two months of publication (or further time allowed) by giving notice of opposition including grounds and terms/conditions of licence they would grant and accompanying evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponent must serve copy of notice and evidence on applicant and notify Controller; no further statements/evidence except with leave; Controller fixes hearing date with not less than ten days' notice; hearing procedure follows sub-rules of rule 62 as far as may apply; if prima facie case not made out Controller notifies applicant who may request hearing within one month; if hearing requested Controller, after opportunity to be heard, determines whether application proceeds and issues speaking order expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions the Controller seeks when settling a licence
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller endeavours to secure that: a) royalty/remuneration is reasonable having regard to nature of invention and expenditure; b) patented invention is worked to fullest extent by licensee with reasonable profit; c) patented articles are available to public at reasonably affordable prices; d) licence is non-exclusive; e) right of licensee is non-assignable; f) licence is for the balance term of patent unless shorter term consistent with public interest; g) licence granted primarily for supply in Indian market though licensee may export if needed; h) for semiconductor technology, licence is to work invention for public noncommercial use; i) where licence remedies anti-competitive practice, licensee may be permitted to export.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms may be revised on application by licensee after not less than twelve months on ground that terms proved more onerous than expected and licensee unable to work except at loss; no second such application allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by licensee to protect customers of applicant (Section 88)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Controller is satisfied that manufacture/use/sale of materials not protected by patent is prejudiced by conditions imposed by patentee upon grant of licences or upon purchase/hire/use of patented article/process, he may order grant of licences under the patent to such customers of the applicant as he thinks fit as well as to the applicant.
